skill.name: skill-auditor
skill.description: Audits skill definitions for structure, quality, completeness, and decomposition needs. Use it to review SKILL.md files, bundled resources, and marketplace readiness before publication.
skill.summary: Audits skill definitions and reports structure, quality, and decomposition issues.
skill.author: BarisSozen

security_audit.summary: All static findings were reviewed as false positives. The Markdown backticks in SKILL.md are documentation or bounded local command examples, and scripts/audit_skills.py line 160 only records a validation error. No prompt injection, exfiltration intent, or malicious behavior was found.

static_findings.snippet: List all skills in the `.claude/skills/` directory:
For each skill directory, verify it contains the required `SKILL.md` file.
- `description`: 50+ characters, specific about triggers, no placeholders
For automated fixes, use the audit script with `--fix` flag:
See `references/audit-criteria.md` for detailed scoring rubrics and decomposition guidelines.

Line 25 opens a fenced bash example for listing a local skills directory. The example is bounded documentation and does not contain dynamic shell interpolation.
Line 27 is only the closing Markdown fence for a local listing example. It contains no executable shell expression.
The backticks on line 29 mark the filename SKILL.md in prose. This is documentation text, not command execution.
Line 35 opens a fenced bash example for running the bundled audit script with a fixed relative path. The referenced script reads local skill files and prints reports without shelling out.
Line 37 is a Markdown fence delimiter after a documented local script command. It is not shell syntax or executable code.
The backticks on line 52 format the frontmatter key name in documentation. No external command or shell substitution is present.
The backticks on line 53 format the description field name in prose. This is safe Markdown formatting, not command execution.
Line 69 opens a plain Markdown report template, not a shell block. The content is an output format example and contains no executable command.
Line 88 is the closing fence for a non-shell report template. It does not execute code or request external commands.
Line 92 uses backticks to format a command-line option in prose. It is not shell backtick execution, and the bundled script does not implement that option.
Line 94 opens a fenced bash example for a local audit script command. The command path is fixed, and the reviewed script has no network, shell execution, or secret access behavior.
Line 96 is only the closing Markdown fence after a local script example. It contains no executable instruction by itself.
The backticks on line 102 format a relative reference file path. This is documentation linking to local criteria, not command execution.
The backticks on line 108 format the bundled script path in the resources list. It does not invoke a shell or interpolate user input.

content.value_statement: Skill libraries can drift into inconsistent formats, weak descriptions, and unclear workflows. This skill combines automated checks with manual review criteria to improve structure and marketplace readiness.
actual_capabilities: Validates SKILL.md frontmatter for name and description fields.
Checks for required sections such as When to Use and Workflow.
Counts words and TODO placeholders in skill content.
Reviews bundled script, reference, and asset directories for basic issues.
Produces human-readable or JSON audit summaries from the bundled script.
Recommends when large or complex skills should be split.
limitations: It focuses on quality and structure, not deep security analysis.
It uses simple text and regex checks, not full YAML or Markdown parsing.
It requires local access to the skill directory being audited.
The documented fix option is not implemented by the bundled script.

use_cases.title: Review a Skill Library
use_cases.description: Audit many local skills before publication and identify repeated structure problems.

use_cases.title: Improve a Draft Skill
use_cases.description: Find missing sections, weak descriptions, and TODO placeholders before sharing a skill.

use_cases.title: Plan Skill Decomposition
use_cases.description: Decide whether a broad skill should be split into smaller focused skills.

prompt_templates.title: Audit One Skill
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a single local skill.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use skill-auditor to review the skill at the provided path. Summarize errors, warnings, score, and the top fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Audit All Skills
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of a local skills directory.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the skill-auditor workflow across my skills directory. Group results by severity and identify common quality problems.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Decomposition
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of scope and structure.
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate whether this skill should be split. Consider word count, workflows, audiences, resource files, and reusable components.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Marketplace Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this skill for marketplace readiness. Provide validation results, content quality notes, decomposition advice, and publication blockers.

output_examples.input: Review a skill with missing Workflow section and a short description.
output_examples.output: The report flags a missing Workflow section, notes the short description, lowers the quality score, and recommends specific edits.

output_examples.input: Audit a directory that contains several complete skills and one draft skill.
output_examples.output: The summary separates passing skills from the draft, lists warnings, and highlights the draft as the main cleanup target.

output_examples.input: Evaluate a long skill with several unrelated responsibilities.
output_examples.output: The review recommends decomposition, explains the scope problems, and proposes smaller skill areas to separate.

best_practices: Run automated validation before manual review so structure issues are visible.
Read SKILL.md and bundled references before judging skill scope.
Tie each recommendation to a clear file, section, or user impact.
anti_patterns: Treating the numeric score as final without reading the skill content.
Auditing only frontmatter while ignoring bundled scripts and references.
Publishing a skill while known TODO placeholders remain in user-facing text.

faq.question: What does this skill audit?
faq.answer: It audits skill structure, frontmatter, required sections, resource directories, word count, placeholders, and decomposition needs.

faq.question: Does it perform a security review?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on quality and structure, not full security analysis or malware detection.

faq.question: Can it audit multiple skills at once?
faq.answer: Yes. The bundled script can scan a local skills directory and report results for each skill.

faq.question: Can it output machine-readable results?
faq.answer: Yes. The script supports JSON output for automation and reporting workflows.

faq.question: Does it automatically fix problems?
faq.answer: No. The bundled script does not implement the documented fix option.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Skill authors, marketplace reviewers, and teams maintaining shared AI skill libraries can use it.
